rationale: The buyer is a named SMB/team on a paid Dropbox Business plan ($15–$24/user/month), so commercial intent exists, and willingness to pay for SaaS tooling is established. The service — automated privacy-policy change monitoring with plain-language risk summaries — is fully buildable and deliverable by Claude with no per-customer human touch. However, the signal is a single low-upvote HN comment, responsiveness is untested, and the pain recurs only when a provider updates its policy (every 1–3 years per vendor), making urgency episodic. Validate by reaching 50–100 Dropbox Business admins (via r/sysadmin, LinkedIn, Hacker News) with a one-question cold message before building.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a SaaS privacy-policy monitor that tracks changes across major cloud storage providers and emails a plain-language risk summary to subscribers whenever a material change is detected. The factory builds it as a Claude-powered diff analyzer (privacy policy text in → structured risk assessment out) paired with a simple landing page, a Stripe subscription link ($9–$19/month), and an automated weekly email digest; no coding required from the operator. To sell, the factory drafts a cold outreach message targeting Dropbox Business admins on LinkedIn and r/sysadmin, which Youval approves before it goes out. Once a subscriber signs up, Claude monitors the policy feeds on a schedule and sends digests automatically; billing runs via Stripe; the operator's only recurring action is approving outreach batches. The honest constraint: policy changes are infrequent, so subscribers may churn if months pass without an alert — validate retention intent before building.
notes: No build_gate failures. Consider bundling multi-provider coverage (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box) to increase perceived value and reduce churn from infrequent alerts.
